title: Olbers' Paradox: Why Is the Sky Dark at Night?
question: If the universe is infinite and full of stars, why does the night sky look mostly dark instead of blazing with light in every direction?
summary: A seemingly trivial observation—that the night sky is dark—turns out to rule out an infinite, static, eternal universe, and points instead toward a universe with a finite age and an expanding, cooling afterglow we now call the cosmic microwave background.
